chapter: California, Cats and the Fiddle, the Tatum trio
title: Pitching Swingin' in the Groove to Armstrong; theme songs; the fish song
summary: He tried to get Louis Armstrong and Louis Jordan to do his song, and describes his closing theme and a fish song sung at a Kleinsinger concert.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Had you written songs before this, for other bands?

Yeah. I like to have two good chances but somehow or other fate let them go. Louis Armstrong was gonna do Swingin In the Groove. And it fitted him perfectly. So was Louis Jordan But my song came up last and by that time
They were tired, they said, "well, we do it next time.
How did you get the song to Louis?

I don't know I think I bugged everybody, ha ha. I just bugged everybody. Didn't nobody write -- I don't think it was wrote out. I believe I hummed it. We had the words wrote. But there was no music, 'cause I don't remember nobody writing no music. But by the time he got to it he had been goin' for about 3 or 4 hours. By hummin' it to him, trying to get him. He liked it all right. But just didn't have the time.
Had you written those tunes for this group? (C+F)

I just wrote 'em just so. For this particular group I had wrote a couple of theme songs one to go on & one to come off. Introduction, you know. We sang and called every body's name & we went off. I still use it when we go off now. George Kells uses it quite a bit.

We hope you like our music, we did the best we could And if you heard your favorite song we hope that it was good We're going but we'll be back so everybody have a drink You have one & I'll have one, it's later than you think.

And I have a fish song that it ever got to Sesame Street or somewhere like that it would go over. It's called 'I don't care how fast a fish may swim that he'll never sweat.' I recorded it in Paris, but it didn't mean anything over there. I never recorded it here but I do it a lot. I did it on a Jack Kleinsinger concert and we had 700 people sing it -- audience participation. 700 people sang 'He'll never sweat.' It goes over good...
